bounds.domain: One process-local CacheClient, one cached value, two reusable in-flight command slots, failure threshold two and cooldown two elapsed ticks. Production uses threshold five and a 60,000 ms cooldown. Elapsed time only advances through 0..3, while wall time may move anywhere in 0..4.
bounds.atomicity: A backend command's mutation and acknowledgement are separate. An acknowledged DEL removes the value, and a lost response can hide a completed delete. Existing commands can settle after the breaker opens.
bounds.progress: An eligible cooldown probe reopens the client under weak fairness while no later failure restarts the cooldown. This does not require successful backend recovery.
bounds.conformance: Named tests run the production CacheClient and Wadis adapter against its actual Redis WASM build. WRONGTYPE and ACL command errors are real. Clocks are controlled separately, and one acknowledgement loss is injected after a real DEL.

limitations: The checked entry points are getWithOutcome and delConfirmed, plus their shared failure/cooldown methods. A successful single-key miss retains failures, while a hit or acknowledged delete resets them. This is the existing heuristic, not a global health authority.

The model starts after backend selection. Network connection initialization, transport reconnects, backend migration, persisted TTL/policy deadlines, cache fills, SWR invalidation races and cross-client coordination remain separate protocols.
Only two overlapping commands and a scaled failure threshold are modeled. Backend correctness and arbitrary caller counts are not proved, and no general TypeScript refinement is claimed.

assumptions: The process remains alive and a continuously eligible cooldown probe is weakly fair.
A later completed failure can restart the wait. Backend success and clock advancement are not guaranteed.
